title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 2.93 (versions follow prime numbers; 293 after 283): she imagines what she never read. Razar's imagination is joined to her improvising: while she plays a piece of her theme, a word that carries something for her (by her own measure) may give its place to another that holds one of its roles in the window she reads (the word before and the word after at once: Razar's definition of alike, read in her text), chosen against her luck among every shared role. It is said only if the clause it makes is written in none of her books nor in their talk. No word list: the alike word comes from her window, and her wish to imagine, (S + 1/2) / (N + 1), is taught by her frame coefficient. Each one imagined is kept in 'imaginado'. Seen in a copy of her house: 'el valor de verdad' of a philosophy book became 'el proposito de verdad', a clause found in none of her books. Stated: one word at a time; the alike word is sought only in the 4 KB window; novelty is checked by reading all her books each time (about 50 MB); the joining forms Razar finds and its open votes are not yet shared; the Windows package is still the one of v2.83. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v2.93: imagina lo que nunca leyó. Prototipo de investigación.
